input.rationale: Section 15.9 selects Delaware law, which is on our accepted fallback list and is left untouched. The forum fails the fallback: Section 15.10.1 sends every unresolved Dispute to mandatory, final and binding ICDR arbitration, and Section 15.10.2.2 both mandates ICDR determination and delegates the scope/applicability question to the tribunal. The seat is New York (domestic), so this is a medium-severity forum deviation, not walk-away. Our three edits submit unresolved Disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware state and federal courts and confine the retained ICDR machinery, including the ICDR's authority over scope, to arbitrations the Parties agree to in writing, so no unqualified arbitration mandate or competence-competence delegation survives to contradict the court clause. We left the intellectual property carve-out to a U.S. federal court of appropriate jurisdiction, the Section 7.5.5 Material Impact route and the preliminary injunctive relief carve-out intact; the IP carve-out is a customary limited-subject-matter forum point that we do not treat as defeating the Delaware merits forum.

proposal.summary: Send unresolved Disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware state and federal courts, and confine the Section 15.10.2 ICDR process (including the ICDR's authority over scope) to arbitrations the Parties agree to in writing.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that disputes are decided by the courts of the governing-law jurisdiction rather than by mandatory arbitration, so we have submitted unresolved Disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware state and federal courts and made the Section 15.10.2 ICDR process, including the ICDR's authority over any question of scope, apply only where the Parties agree in writing to arbitrate. Delaware law under Section 15.9, the executive escalation period, the Section 7.5.5 Material Impact route, the intellectual property carve-out and the preliminary injunctive relief carve-out are all unchanged.

ops.oldText: then such Dispute shall be submitted to the International Centre for Dispute Resolution ("ICDR") for final and binding arbitration pursuant to the arbitration clause set forth in Section 15.10.2.
ops.newText: then such Dispute shall be resolved exclusively by the state and federal courts located in the State of Delaware, and each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of those courts.

ops.oldText: Either Party shall have the right to initiate arbitration at any time after the expiration of thirty (30) days after a Dispute is notified to the Executive Officers.
ops.newText: A Dispute may be referred to arbitration under this Section 15.10.2 only if both Parties so agree in writing after the Dispute has arisen.

ops.oldText: Any Dispute including the determination of the scope or applicability of this agreement to arbitrate, shall be determined by the ICDR in accordance with its International Arbitration Rules, except as they may be modified herein.
ops.newText: Where the Parties have agreed in writing to arbitrate under Section 15.10.2.1, such Dispute shall be determined by the ICDR in accordance with its International Arbitration Rules, except as they may be modified herein.
